Flat and nested weighted stochastic block models with edge covariates

weighted_block_state.Rd

Construct, evaluate, and infer flat and hierarchical (nested) weighted stochastic block models (Peixoto 2018) supporting all five graph-tool edge covariate distributions (real-exponential, real-normal, discrete-geometric, discrete-poisson, and discrete-binomial), multiple simultaneous covariates, and both microcanonical and Bayesian conjugate hyperpriors.

Usage

weighted_block_state(graph, weights, types, params = "microcanonical",
  blocks = NULL, degree_corrected = TRUE,
  degree_prior = c("distributed", "uniform"))
weighted_description_length(state, rec = TRUE, rec_dl = TRUE,
  degree_prior = NULL)
minimize_weighted_blockmodel_dl(graph, weights, types,
  params = "microcanonical", degree_corrected = TRUE,
  degree_prior = c("distributed", "uniform"), B_min = 1L, B_max = Inf,
  refine = TRUE, epsilon = 1e-3, nthreads = NULL)
nested_weighted_block_state(graph, weights, types, params = "microcanonical",
  levels = NULL, degree_corrected = TRUE,
  degree_prior = c("distributed", "uniform"))
nested_weighted_level_entropy(state, degree_prior = NULL)
nested_weighted_description_length(state, degree_prior = NULL)
minimize_nested_weighted_blockmodel_dl(graph, weights, types,
  params = "microcanonical", degree_corrected = TRUE,
  degree_prior = c("distributed", "uniform"), B_min = 1L, B_max = Inf,
  refine = TRUE, epsilon = 1e-3, nthreads = NULL)

Arguments

graph

A graph created by graph_create.

weights

Edge covariate values: either a character vector naming one or more edge properties stored on graph, a numeric vector of length graph_num_edges(graph), an \(E \times K\) numeric matrix, or a list mixing property names and numeric vectors.

types

Character vector of length \(K\) naming the covariate model for each column of weights: "real-exponential", "real-normal", "discrete-geometric", "discrete-poisson", or "discrete-binomial".

params

Covariate hyperprior specification: "microcanonical" (default, Peixoto 2018 maximum-entropy microcanonical priors), "bayesian" (empirical-Bayes conjugate hyperpriors matching graph-tool), a named list of hyperparameters (e.g. list(alpha = 1, beta = 2) or list(N = 10, alpha = 1, beta = 1) or list(m0 = 0, k0 = 1, v0 = 1, nu0 = 3)), or a list of length \(K\) specifying one entry per covariate.

blocks

Optional 1-based integer group membership vector of length graph_num_vertices(graph).

levels

Optional non-empty list of 1-based integer label vectors for each hierarchy level.

degree_corrected

Whether to use the degree-corrected (TRUE) or non-degree-corrected (FALSE) topology model.

degree_prior

Degree sequence hyperprior ("distributed" or "uniform").

state

A rgraphtool_weighted_block_state or rgraphtool_nested_weighted_block_state object.

rec

Whether to include the edge-covariate log-likelihood term.

rec_dl

Whether to include the global covariate hyperprior description length term.

B_min, B_max

Minimum and maximum number of occupied level-0 groups.

refine

Whether to run greedy local refinement sweeps.

epsilon

Convergence tolerance in nats.

nthreads

Optional thread count override (defaults to rgraphtool_num_threads()).

Details

All description lengths match graph-tool 3.9's WeightedBlockState and NestedBlockState(base_state=WeightedBlockState) to machine precision (including the exact continuous quantization scale \(\epsilon = 0.1 \min_{w_e \neq 0} |w_e|\) and the nested real-normal variance hyperprior).

Weighted states integrate directly with block_membership, block_sizes, nested_levels, nested_project, nested_summary, plot_hierarchy, mcmc_sweep, mcmc_equilibrate, mcmc_anneal, sample_posterior, and model_evidence.

Value

Flat constructors and minimizers return a rgraphtool_weighted_block_state; nested constructors and minimizers return a rgraphtool_nested_weighted_block_state. Description length functions return a numeric scalar (or per-level numeric vector for nested_weighted_level_entropy()).

References

Peixoto, T. P. (2018). Nonparametric weighted stochastic block models. Physical Review E 97, 012306.

See also

compare_weight_models, transform_weights, graph_set_edge_property, demo("weighted_sbm")

Examples

set.seed(42)
g <- graph_create(12, directed = FALSE)
edges <- rbind(t(utils::combn(1:6, 2)), t(utils::combn(7:12, 2)), c(6, 7))
w <- c(stats::rnorm(15, 5, 0.5), stats::rnorm(15, -5, 0.5), 0)
graph_add_edges(g, edges, properties = list(w = w))
st <- minimize_weighted_blockmodel_dl(g, weights = "w", types = "real-normal")
st
#> <weighted block state: degree-corrected, real-normal, B = 2, description length 76.6180 nats>
nst <- minimize_nested_weighted_blockmodel_dl(g, weights = "w",
                                              types = "real-normal")
nst
#> <nested weighted block state: degree-corrected, real-normal, 2 levels, B = 2-1, description length 86.0293 nats>
